What marks the onset of puberty?
questions.a: Hormones wake the reproductive organs; boys and girls develop secondary sexual characters and can reproduce.

questions.q: At what ages does puberty usually arrive in boys and girls?
questions.a: About 11-13 years in girls and 12-14 in boys, varying child to child.

questions.q: Name the glands that control puberty changes.
questions.a: The pituitary master gland, and the testes/ovaries which release testosterone and oestrogen.

concepts.title: Physical Changes and Voice Box Development

questions.q: Why does a boy's voice become deeper at puberty?
questions.a: The larynx (voice box) grows bigger, so vocal cords lengthen and the voice deepens.

questions.q: Name two changes that occur only in girls at puberty.
questions.a: Breasts develop and the menstrual cycle begins (hips also widen).

questions.q: What is Adam's apple?
questions.a: The bulge on a grown boy's throat caused by the enlarged larynx.

questions.q: What are secondary sexual characters?
questions.a: Features that mark the sexes but are not reproductive organs - facial hair in boys, breast development in girls, pubic hair in both.

questions.q: Name the hormone responsible for male secondary characters.
questions.a: Testosterone, made by the testes.

questions.q: Which hormone brings about female secondary characters?
questions.a: Oestrogen, released by the ovaries.

questions.q: Which gland is called the master gland and why?
questions.a: The pituitary - its hormones direct other endocrine glands, including the reproductive glands at puberty.

questions.q: How do hormones start the reproductive phase of life?
questions.a: At puberty the pituitary signals testes/ovaries, which pour sex hormones that begin sperm or egg production and body changes.

questions.q: Name the hormones released by testes and ovaries.
questions.a: Testes: testosterone. Ovaries: oestrogen and progesterone.

concepts.title: Female Reproductive Phase and Menstrual Cycle

questions.q: What is the menstrual cycle?
questions.a: A monthly cycle in which the uterine lining thickens for a possible pregnancy and sheds as blood if no egg is fertilised.

questions.q: How long does one menstrual cycle usually last?
questions.a: About 28 days, but it varies from woman to woman.

questions.q: When does menstruation usually begin and stop?
questions.a: It begins at puberty (menarche, around 11-13) and stops at menopause (45-50 years).

questions.q: How many chromosome pairs does a human body cell have?
questions.a: 23 pairs - 46 chromosomes in all.

questions.q: Which chromosomes decide a baby's sex?
questions.a: The sex chromosomes: females XX, males XY.

questions.q: Why is a mother not responsible for the sex of her child?
questions.a: She always gives an X chromosome; the father's sperm brings X (girl) or Y (boy).

concepts.title: Other Endocrine Glands and Their Hormones

questions.q: Name the hormones of the thyroid and adrenal glands.
questions.a: Thyroid: thyroxine (needs iodine). Adrenal: adrenaline (emergency hormone).

questions.q: What happens when the thyroid makes too little thyroxine?
questions.a: A goitre (swollen neck) can develop - often caused by lack of iodine in food.

questions.q: What does growth hormone do and where is it made?
questions.a: It controls height and body growth; the pituitary makes it.

questions.q: How do hormones control metamorphosis in frogs?
questions.a: Thyroxine from the thyroid makes the tadpole change into a frog.

questions.q: Why must tadpole water contain iodine for normal change into frogs?
questions.a: Thyroxine needs iodine; without it metamorphosis stops and tadpoles stay tadpoles.

questions.q: Which insect hormone controls its change from larva to adult?
questions.a: Insect hormones guide moulting and the pupa's change into the adult.

questions.q: Why is personal hygiene vital during adolescence?
questions.a: Sweat glands work harder and secretions increase, so daily bathing and clean clothes prevent body odour and infections.

questions.q: What diet keeps adolescents healthy?
questions.a: A balanced diet rich in protein, calcium, iron and vitamins, plus plenty of water.

questions.q: Name one habit adolescents must avoid and one they must adopt.
questions.a: Avoid drugs, smoking and junk food; adopt regular exercise, enough sleep and honest talk about changes with elders.
